messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Incident detected: cross-region routing oscillation affecting inference gateway. Symptom: requests bouncing between us-east <-> us-west <-> eu with elevated 503s and token latency spikes. Alerts: 5xx-rate > 6% across proxy-layer; routing failures increased 300%. Dashboards: https://dash.redwood.local/d/route/health?orgId=1
oncall-alex: I'm up. paging in SRE and runtime. Jam, Maya — you're paged. Anyone oncall in eu?
sre-jamie: On it. grabbing runbook. first step: collect healthcheck events and routing decisions for last 20m. Alex can you grab the routing logs and kv-cache health?
oncall-alex: Pulling now. running: 
```
curl -s "https://api.redwood.local/internal/routes/current?since=20m" | jq '.routes[] | {from,to,decision,reason | .}'
```
Got a lot of rapid fallbacks. sample: 
```
{"from":"us-east","to":"us-west","decision":"fallback","reason":"health-flap"}
{"from":"us-west","to":"eu","decision":"fallback","reason":"health-flap"}
{"from":"eu","to":"us-east","decision":"fallback","reason":"health-flap"}
```
sre-jamie: OK that's the sawtooth. Maya can you check if any recent rollout touched the fallback policy or health-check config?
eng-runtime-maya: I rolled a small change 30m ago to routing engine (optimize path selection). It shouldn't touch health checks but I did tweak policy evaluation order. Looking at the commit: 
```
commit 9f3a2b
 - prefer-local -> prefer-latency order change
 - add aggressive fallback window ms=5000
```
That aggressive fallback window looks suspect. I didn't expect it to apply globally (should be per-customer).
infra-luis: From infra side, I see increased failed health probes from eu->lb backends. Probe logs show alternating pass/fail with ~6s period. Example: 
```
[eu-probe-12] 2026-03-15T02:10:01Z HEALTHCHECK ok
[eu-probe-12] 2026-03-15T02:10:07Z HEALTHCHECK fail code=502
[eu-probe-12] 2026-03-15T02:10:13Z HEALTHCHECK ok
```
That matches a 6s window -> matches Maya's aggressive fallback 5s TTL.
oncall-alex: Customer impact? Any production customers paged?
product-oliver: Not yet escalated by customers but we have elevated error rates for enterprise customers in EU and US. Preliminary impact: p95 latency +400ms and error rate spike to 4-8% depending on endpoint. Two customers (acme-corp, finlytics) reported degraded quality via support. Need a concise impact blurb for execs.
sre-jamie: Triage plan: 1) Stop the oscillation (mitigate) 2) Rollback or patch config to prevent re-flap 3) Run canaries and monitor 4) Postmortem. Immediate mitigation: disable aggressive fallback window or increase healthcheck stable window to 30s. Alex, can you toggle policy to conservative mode?
oncall-alex: On it. Executing rollback toggle via admin API: 
```
# switch to conservative routing policy (panic-disable aggressive fallback)
POST /admin/routing/policy/override  {"policy":"conservative","reason":"incident-3332101111-mitigate"}
```
response: 200 OK. applying to global routing.
incident-bot: action logged: routing.policy.override executed by oncall-alex at 2026-03-15T02:12:05Z
sre-jamie: Good. infra Luis — can you throttle health probe frequency from 5s -> 30s for eu and us-west, and add 3-success consecutive requirement?
infra-luis: Applying change to probe config now. patch: 
```
probe.interval = 10s
probe.failure_threshold = 3
probe.success_threshold = 3
```
Rolled to eu/us-west; us-east left as-is. Rolling change tool output: "patch applied to eu cluster 3/3, us-west 2/2"
eng-runtime-maya: I'm going to revert the policy commit to be safe. creating revert PR and will push canary to non-prod first.
eng-runtime-maya: PR merged and canary deployed to staging. No flaps in staging. Ready to promote to canary prod group.
sre-jamie: After Alex's override and Luis' probe change we're seeing stabilization in routing decisions. Sample from routing log: 
```
2026-03-15T02:15:12Z route decision: us-east -> us-east keep reason=healthy
2026-03-15T02:15:20Z route decision: us-west -> us-west keep reason=healthy
```
error rate trending down: 5xx now 0.8% (was 6.2%).
product-oliver: Can you confirm whether any requests were served by wrong model variant (fallback served a quantized variant causing regressions)? Need to know for customer-facing notes.
eng-runtime-maya: Quick check: routing fallback only moved traffic between same model family (gptx-4 variants). No variant downgrade observed in logs. We did see some transient KV-cache misses causing token retries but not model downgrade.
incident-bot: incident state changed: mitigation_in_progress -> stabilized at 2026-03-15T02:18:30Z
oncall-alex: Paging escalation: I'm handing off to infra-luis for post-incident patch and rollback verification. Luis — you're owning until 04:00 UTC.
infra-luis: Ack. I'll keep monitoring for next 2 hours and run synthetic tests.
sre-jamie: Immediate actions to include in follow-up: 
- revert commit 9f3a2b from runtime (Maya)
- change default fallback window from 5s -> 30s
- add per-region probe backoff and 3-success requirement
- add rate-limited circuit breaker to routing decisions to avoid rapid oscillation
- add synthetic heartbeat that exercises regional routing every 60s with alert if flip > 3 in 10m

product-oliver: Requested impact summary for CS/execs: 
"Between 02:05-02:18 UTC we observed a cross-region routing oscillation that produced elevated 5xx (peak 6.2%) and increased p95 latency by ~400ms for impacted regions (EU, US-West). Two enterprise customers reported degraded responses; no model downgrade detected. Mitigation (02:12-02:18): policy override + probe tuning. Service stabilized; monitoring will continue for 2h. Postmortem scheduled"
eng-runtime-maya: I'll open the PR to revert and add telemetry around policy scope (global vs per-customer).
incident-bot: post:runbook:incident-3332101111 created by oncall-alex
oncall-alex: Closing the immediate incident thread. Luis, please send final "resolved" message after 2h observation window. Thanks all for fast reaction. :thumbsup:
infra-luis: Observing window complete at 04:20 UTC. No repeat flaps. Marking incident resolved. Follow-ups created: 
- CRT-142: revert 9f3a2b and add guardrails (owner: maya)
- CRT-143: probe backoff defaults audit (owner: luis)
- CRT-144: add routing flip synthetic checks (owner: jamie)

product-oliver: Sending customer note now.
incident-bot: incident state changed: stabilized -> resolved at 2026-03-15T04:20:15Z by infra-luis
